'''V. Narry Kim''' ({{Korean|hangul=김빛내리}}; born 18 June 1969<ref>{{cite web|title=한국과학기술한림원 - 회원 - 회원소개|url=https://kast.or.kr/kr/member/member_view.php?idx=4827|website=Korean Academy of Science and Technology|language=ko|access-date=7 January 2026}}</ref>) is a South Korean biochemist and microbiologist, best known for her work on [[microRNA]] [[biogenesis]]. Her pioneering studies have laid the groundwork for the biology of microRNA and contributed to the improvement of [[RNA interference]] technologies.

==Background==
Kim was born in South Korea in 1969. Kim first became interested in science as a high school student. When asked why she chose science as a lifelong career, she said, “I was charmed by the simplicity of the principles underlying the complexity of life.”<ref name="narrykim.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.narrykim.org/legacy/QuestInterview.pdf |title=Interview |website=www.narrykim.org |access-date=2014-12-16 |archive-date=2016-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303234811/http://www.narrykim.org/legacy/QuestInterview.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Education==
Kim went on to pursue a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] degree in [[microbiology]], then followed by a [[Master of Science|MS]] degree in microbiology in 1992 and 1994, respectively, both from [[Seoul National University]] (SNU). After completing her masters under adviser Kang Sa-Ouk, Kim went to the United Kingdom to further her studies at the [[University of Oxford]], studying the functions of retroviral proteins under Alan J. Kingsman.<ref>{{cite magazine |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title= V. Narry Kim: Embracing the Challenge of Science |url= https://www.thermofisher.com/content/dam/LifeTech/migration/en/filelibrary/pdf/quest.par.65555.file.dat/quest%202.1.pdf |magazine= Quest |publisher= Thermo Fisher Scientific |date= March 2005 |access-date= 24 January 2019 |page = 31 |quote = I have long been interested in noncoding RNAs since my graduate days in Alan Kingsman’s lab at Oxford University, even though my doctoral thesis was on retroviruses.}}</ref><ref name=":cell"/> She graduated with a PhD in [[biochemistry]] in 1998.

==Career==
Her academic journey then took her to the United States, where she took a position at the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in Philadelphia as a research assistant. 
After completing her postdoctoral research on [[mRNA surveillance]] in the laboratory of [[Gideon Dreyfuss]],<ref name=":ibio">{{cite web |url= https://www.ibiology.org/speakers/v-narry-kim/ |title= V Narry Kim - iBiology |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= iBiology |access-date= 24 January 2019 }}</ref> Kim finished her postdoctoral studies and returned to Korea in 2001. She then started working at [[Seoul National University]] as a research assistant professor. By the age of 35, Kim already had twenty-two of her papers published in well known and prestigious scientific publications, such as ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' and ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''. In addition, Kim “holds four patents based on her research activities, including one on a novel HIV-based gene delivery vector.”<ref name="narrykim.org"/>

In 2008, she became an associate professor, then a SNU Distinguished Fellow in 2010, and a full professor in 2013. Located in Seoul National University, she began working with the [[Institute for Basic Science]] (IBS) in 2012 as the founding director of the Center for RNA Research. her lab focuses on RNA-mediated gene regulation research, specifically investigating post-transcriptional gene regulation mediated by [[microRNAs]] (miRNAs).<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ibs.re.kr/eng/sub02_05_03.do |title= Center for RNA Research - Life Sciences - Research Centers|author=<!--Not stated--> |website= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |access-date= 24 January 2019 |quote= Our research center is currently conducting research on microRNAs and other ncRNAs using cancer and stem cells as model systems. In addition, our center is running a long-term project to systematically identify novel ncRNAs and proteins that bind to them. These studies will advance our understanding of cellular regulatory mechanisms and provide a conceptual basis for the development of new therapies and diagnostic techniques.}}</ref> The lab employs biochemistry, molecular biology, genetic, biophysical, and computational approaches. Research is focused on miRNAs, which are small non-coding RNAs involved in practically all working aspects of eukaryotic cells. Tight control of miRNA is vital to normal functioning cells. If dysregulated, miRNAs can often be linked to human diseases such as cancer. By focusing on the miRNA biogenesis, Dr. Kim's lab has made major contributions to the understanding of miRNAs are created and processed in animal cells. These studies can potentially open the doors to new forms of cancer treatment and stem cell engineering.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.narrykim.org/en/home|title=RNA Biology: Narry Kim Lab|website=www.narrykim.org}}</ref>

In 2013, Kim, along with Professor Jin-Soo KIM of the SNU Department of Chemistry developed a new technology to eliminate specific microRNAs. This new technology has the promise of being potentially used to cure cancer and other illnesses in the future. In the research, [[Transcription activator-like effector nuclease|TALENs]] (enzymes) were used to separate certain microRNA from a cell. TALENs had been used to create protein before, but this was the first time they have been used to separate microRNA. The team developed 540 different TALENs for this specific purpose. When this was applied to cancer cells, the proliferation rate of cancer cells dropped to one third of what it was.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.snu.ac.kr/media-coverage?bm=v&bbsidx=119498|title=Professor V. Narry KIM Develops Selective RNA Elimination - Media Coverage - SNU Media - News & Forum - SNU|first=SEOUL NATIONAL|last=UNIVERSITY|website=en.snu.ac.kr}}</ref> This discovery was published in the November 11, 2013 edition of ''[[Nature Structural & Molecular Biology|Nature Structural and Molecular Biology]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Kim |first1= Young-Kook |last2= Wee |first2= Gabbine |last3= Park |first3= Joha |last4= Kim |first4= Jongkyu |last5= Baek |first5= Daehyun |last6= Kim |first6= Jin-Soo |last7= Kim |first7= V Narry |date= 10 November 2013 |title= TALEN-based knockout library for human microRNAs |url= https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258430311 |journal= Nature Structural & Molecular Biology |volume= 20 |issue= 12 |pages= 1458–1464 |doi= 10.1038/nsmb.2701 |pmid= 24213537 |s2cid= 10448024 |access-date= 24 January 2019}}</ref>

Kim's first paper as PI was published in 2002 in the ''[[EMBO Journal]]''.<ref name="pmid12198168">{{Cite journal|vauthors=Lee Y, Jeon K, Lee JT, Kim S, Kim VN | title = MicroRNA maturation: stepwise processing and subcellular localization | journal = EMBO J. | volume = 21 | issue = 17 | pages = 4663–4670 |date=September 2002 | pmid = 12198168 | doi = 10.1093/emboj/cdf476 | pmc=126204}}</ref> In this highly cited work, she defined two separate processing steps (primary microRNA (pri-miRNA) processing in the nucleus and pre-miRNA processing in the cytoplasm), and proposed a model of the microRNA biogenesis pathway for the first time. Based on this model, her research group discovered that most microRNA genes are transcribed by [[RNA polymerase II]] and that pri-miRNA processing is carried out by [[Drosha]]-DGCR8 complexes in the nucleus.

Her research group further identified uridylation-meditated pre-miRNA degradation pathway by [[LIN28]]<ref name="pmid18951094">{{Cite journal|vauthors=Heo I, Joo C, Cho J, Ha M, Han J, Kim VN | title = Lin28 mediates the terminal uridylation of let-7 precursor MicroRNA | journal = Mol. Cell | volume = 32 | issue = 2 | pages = 276–284 |date=October 2008 | pmid = 18951094 | doi = 10.1016/j.molcel.2008.09.014 | doi-access = free }}</ref> and TUT4,<ref name="pmid19703396">{{Cite journal|vauthors=Heo I, Joo C, Kim YK, Ha M, Yoon MJ, Cho J, Yeom KH, Han J, Kim VN | title = TUT4 in concert with Lin28 suppresses microRNA biogenesis through pre-microRNA uridylation | journal = Cell | volume = 138 | issue = 4 | pages = 696–708 |date=August 2009 | pmid = 19703396 | doi = 10.1016/j.cell.2009.08.002 | s2cid = 15469064 | doi-access = free }}</ref> contributing to a better understanding of how microRNA-mediated gene expression regulation is involved in embryonic stem cell maintenance and cancer cell development. She also discovered the molecular basis for pri-miRNA recognition and cleavage by the Drosha-DGCR8 complexes,<ref name="pmid16751099">{{Cite journal|vauthors=Han J, Lee Y, Yeom KH, Nam JW, Heo I, Rhee JK, Sohn SY, Cho Y, Zhang BT, Kim VN | title = Molecular basis for the recognition of primary microRNAs by the Drosha-DGCR8 complex | journal = Cell | volume = 125 | issue = 5 | pages = 887–901 |date=June 2006 | pmid = 16751099 | doi = 10.1016/j.cell.2006.03.043 | s2cid = 453021 | doi-access = free }}</ref> and pre-miRNA processing by Dicer.<ref name="pmid21753850">{{Cite journal|vauthors=Park JE, Heo I, Tian Y, Simanshu DK, Chang H, Jee D, Patel DJ, Kim VN | title = Dicer recognizes the 5' end of RNA for efficient and accurate processing | journal = Nature | volume = 475 | issue = 7355 | pages = 201–205 |date=July 2011 | pmid = 21753850 | doi = 10.1038/nature10198 | pmc = 4693635 }}</ref> These findings suggested several critical points to be considered for designing more efficient [[short hairpin RNA]] (shRNA) vectors and also contributed to the improvement of RNA interference technologies.

The research team led by Narry Kim and Chang Hyeshik confirmed the predicted subgenomic RNAs of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] along with new RNA and dozens of unknown subgenomic RNAs.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Kim |first1= Dongwan |last2= Lee |first2= Joo-Yeon |last3= Yang |first3= Jeong-Sun |last4= Kim |first4= Jun Won |last5= Kim |first5= Kim V. Narry |last6= Chang |first6= Hyeshik |date= 14 May 2020 |title= The Architecture of SARS-CoV-2 Transcriptome |journal= Cell |volume= 181 |issue= 4 |pages= 914–921.e10 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2020.04.011|pmid= 32330414 |pmc= 7179501 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ibs.re.kr/cop/bbs/BBSMSTR_000000000738/selectBoardArticle.do?nttId=18344 |title= New Coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) Mapped Out: A high resolution gene map reveals many viral RNAs with unknown functions and modifications |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |access-date= 10 June 2020 }}</ref> The interdisciplinary team was composed of virologists, microbiologists and computational scientists.<ref>{{cite journal |url= https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-01465-8 |title= South Korea's Institute for Basic Science faces review: Decisions about the country's research flagship will signpost national priorities. |author= Mark Zastrow |date= 27 May 2020 |journal= [[Nature Research]] |volume= 581 |issue= 7809 |pages= S53 |doi= 10.1038/d41586-020-01465-8 |s2cid= 218898089 |access-date= 10 June 2020 |url-access= subscription }}</ref>

Kim received [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oreal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science]] (2008),<ref name="unesco-2008">{{cite web|publisher=UNESCO|title=Tenth anniversary of the L'ORÉAL-UNESCO Awards For Women in Science| url=http://portal.unesco.org/geography/en/ev.php-URL_ID=8354&URL_DO=DO_TOPIC&URL_SECTION=201.html|access-date=2012-01-14}}</ref> [[Ho-Am Prize in Medicine]] (2009)<ref name="hoam-2009">{{cite web|publisher=Ho-Am Foundation|title=The Ho-Am Prize Laureates| url=http://hoamprize.samsungfoundation.org/eng/prize/prizewinner.asp|access-date=2012-01-14}}</ref> and [[Top Scientist and Technologist Award of Korea]] (2013). She is an active member of the RNA Society and the International Society of Stem Cell Research (ISSCR). In addition she has been recognized as one of the top Asian scientists to watch by ''[[Asian Scientist]]''<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.asianscientist.com/2011/05/list/v-narry-kim/ |title= The Ultimate List Of 15 Asian Scientists To Watch – V Narry Kim |last= Chan |first= Juliana |date= 15 May 2011 |website= Asian Scientist |access-date= 24 January 2019 }}</ref> and among the "science stars of East Asia" by ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |title= Science stars of East Asia: From artificial intelligence to infectious diseases, top researchers in Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea and Taiwan are making big impacts on the global stage. |last1= Cyranoski |first1= David |last2= Law |first2= Yao-Hua |last3= Ong |first3= Sandy |last4= Phillips |first4= Nicky |last5= Zastrow |first5= Mark |date= 27 June 2018 |journal= [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume= 558 |issue= 7711 |pages= 502–510 |doi= 10.1038/d41586-018-05506-1 |pmid= 29950631 |doi-access= free }}</ref> She was a [[Clarivate Analytics]] Highly Cited Researcher in the field of molecular biology and genetics in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.ibs.re.kr/cop/bbs/BBSMSTR_000000000739/selectBoardArticle.do?nttId=16529 |title= IBS Places First Among Korean Institutions by Featuring 9 Scientists in List of Highly Cited Researchers |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 4 December 2018 |website= [[Institute for Basic Science]] |access-date= 12 February 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://chem.korea.ac.kr/media/7785 |title= [김종승 교수] 노벨상 후보 도전할 만한 韓 연구자는 '40여명' - 2018.05.14. |last= 강 |first= 민구 |date= 22 November 2018 |website= Department of Chemistry |publisher= [[Korea University]] |access-date= 12 February 2019 |language= ko}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.zdnet.co.kr/view/?no=20151015111617 |title= 세계적으로 영향력이 큰 국내 과학자는 누구? 제7회 지식창조대상에서 최장욱 카이스트 교수 등 10명 선정 |last= 안 |first= 희정 |date= 15 October 2015 |website= ZDNet Korea |access-date= 12 February 2019 |language= ko}}</ref>
